newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-UNSETTLED INTER SEEK UEFA CONSOLATION PRIZE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNSETTLED INTER SEEK UEFA CONSOLATION PRIZE.

text.p: Inter, unsettled by a row involving Dutchman Aron Winter and departing coach Roy Hodgson, meet Anderlecht of Belgium on Tuesday in a UEFA cup quarter-final which could kill off their season.

That is the worst-case scenario for the Milan club and, their task eased by the cushion of an away goal in the first leg 1-1 draw, it probably will not turn out that way against an unchanged Anderlecht suffering scoring problems.
Inter could also be far more motivated.

A few weeks ago, when they were neck and neck with Parma behind runaway leaders Juventus, most Inter players were saying confidently that the UEFA Cup was secondary to the league and the chance of securing a European Cup place.
After losing 1-0 to Parma on Saturday, that notion appears to have vanished with their domestic Cup hopes. Inter are now fourth, 10 points behind Juventus and five adrift of Parma.
"On Tuesday, our season is at stake," said veteran captain Giuseppe Bergomi, recognising that the UEFA Cup is now their only real remaining target in a disappointing season.
Anderlecht would be wise to prepare for the worst. Inter last won the UEFA Cup in 1993-94 when the club was in organisational disarray and finished 13th in the league.
Anderlecht drew some confidence from a 3-1 weekend victory over Sint-Truiden and are fifth in Belgium, with little hope of catching leaders Club Brugge 11 points ahead.
Dutch coach Johan Boskamp listened in on his radio from hospital where he was having kidney stones dealt with.
He could perhaps commiserate with Inter's Winter, who watched the Parma match from the stands with the official reason given being that he was too sick to play.
However, the player looked fine to most observers and Hodgson later admitted that he had been banished after a sarcastic remark about his team selection.
Hodgson stressed that Winter would still be considered for the Anderlecht game although he was happy with the team which turned out at Parma and was unlucky not to draw.

The unrest led Bergomi to appeal to club president Massimo Moratti to intervene. "We are going through an unusual situation because the coach is leaving," he said. Hodgson has already announced he is joining England's Blackburn.
"That isn't a problem for me but merely a greater stimulus. But not all the players see it that way," Bergomi said.
Inter (probable) - Gianluca Pagliuca; Jocelyn Angloma, Massimo Paganin, Salvatore Fresi, Alessandro Pistone, Javier Zanetti, Paul Ince, Ciriaco Sforza, Youri Djorkaeff, Ivan Zamorano, Marco Branca.
Anderlecht - Geert De Vlieger; Olivier Doll, Samuel Johnson, Suad Katana, Celestine Babayaro; Tibor Selymes, Danny Boffin, Johan Walem, Par Zetterberg, Bruno Versavel; Yaw Preko.
